files.detail: Replaced the `beforeRegisterNodeDef` + `chainCallback(prototype,'onNodeCreated')` registration with `comfy.defs.extend('FastPreview', b => ...)`. The whole frame-correlation apparatus — the module-level `execId`, the unfiltered `executing` listener, the `b_preview_with_metadata`/`b_preview` `addEventListener` pair, the `serverSupportsFeature('supports_preview_metadata')` probe and the matching `removeEventListener` cleanup — is deleted in favour of `b.onPreview`, which delivers frames already correlated to the owning node. `node.imgs = [img]` + `setDirtyCanvas` became a `node.widgets.canvas({ draw })` surface plus `redraw()`; `setSize([550,550])` became `setSize({width,height})`. Per-node state moved to a Map keyed by node.id, cleared in `b.onRemoved`.
files.test:
equivalence: A FastPreview node is created at 550x550 and, when a preview frame arrives that is addressed to that node, the frame's image is rendered on the node. Passes on both the original (b_preview_with_metadata whose displayNodeId matches the node id -> node.imgs = [img], setDirtyCanvas) and the converted source (b.onPreview -> state.img set, canvas widget redrawn). Also: after the node is removed, a subsequent preview frame for that id renders nothing and leaks no listener.

fix: With TWO FastPreview nodes previewing in the same run on a server that does NOT advertise supports_preview_metadata, a plain `b_preview` frame is attributed to exactly one node — the one the backend is executing. On the ORIGINAL this fails: every FastPreview instance registers its own global `b_preview` listener and each compares the single module-level `execId` against its own id, so the frame is shown on whichever node id happens to equal execId while the other node's stale image is left in place; worse, because `execId` is module-global and updated by an unfiltered "executing" listener, a frame emitted after execId has advanced is mis-attributed to the newly-executing node even if the frame belongs to the previous one. On the CONVERTED source b.onPreview delivers the frame already correlated to the owning node, so attribution is per-node and cannot be raced by a shared global.

files.detail:
Four distinct published-API gaps, spanning every case in the file; converting the remainder would leave prototype patches behind and fail retires-the-old-surface, so the file punts whole.

(1) NO CLICK HANDLER FOR A BUTTON WIDGET. `WidgetDef` is `{type,name,value?,options?,disabled?,hidden?,serialize?}` — there is no `callback`/`onClick` member. The only listener channel is `WidgetHandle.on('change', ...)`, and its bridge (`notify` in widgetHandle.ts) opens with `if (value === previous) return`. A button click invokes litegraph's callback WITHOUT mutating `widget.value`, so the change listener provably never fires for a button. This kills all three button sites: setupDynamicInputs' `addWidget("button","Update inputs",null,rebuild)`, the `Set all` button on FluxBlockLoraSelect/HunyuanVideoBlockLoraSelect/Wan21BlockLoraSelect/LTX2BlockLoraSelect, and SoundReactive's `Start mic capture` / `Stop mic capture`. `NodeDefBuilder.addMenuItem` is a context-menu entry, not an on-node button, so it is not equivalent. NEEDED: a `callback`/`onClick` on `WidgetDef` for `type:'button'`, or a `'click'` event on `WidgetHandle.on`.

(2) NO PER-WIDGET CUSTOM SERIALIZER. Case 5 (SaveImageKJ, SaveImageWithAlpha, SaveStringKJ, DecodeAndSaveVideo, ModelSaveKJ, LoraExtractKJ) does `widget.serializeValue = () => applyTextReplacements(app, widget.value)` on `filename_prefix`. `WidgetDef.serialize` is a BOOLEAN only — include or omit — and `NodeDefBuilder.onSerialize` merges pack-owned keys into the serialized node and explicitly cannot write core fields, so it cannot rewrite `widgets_values`. This is prompt-visible, not cosmetic: dropping it sends `%date:yyyy-MM-dd%`-style tokens to the backend unexpanded and changes the filename actually written to disk. Secondary gap: `applyTextReplacements` itself is only on `window.comfyAPI.utils` and has no published equivalent, so even given a serializer hook the substitution has no published implementation. NEEDED: `WidgetDef.serialize` accepting a function, plus a published text-replacement helper.

(3) NO SLOT SHAPE. `SlotCollection.add(name, type)` takes no options object, and `SlotPatch` is `{name?,label?,type?}` — no `shape`. setupDynamicInputs is called with `slotOptions:{shape:7}` (RenderShape.HOLLOW_CIRCLE, the optional-input marker) for ImageBatchMulti, ImageAddMulti, CrossFadeImagesMulti, TransitionImagesMulti, ImageConcatMulti and JoinStringMulti. Slot `shape` is carried in the serialized node's `inputs` array, so silently dropping it is a workflow wire-format change as well as a visual one. NEEDED: an options argument on `SlotCollection.add` and a `shape` field on `SlotPatch`.

(4) WIDGET CHANGE LISTENER CANNOT DISTINGUISH INTERACTIVE FROM PROGRAMMATIC. setupDynamicInputs wraps `countW.callback = function(value, canvas){ ...; if (!canvas) rebuild(); }` and the file documents the intent: the litegraph `canvas` second argument is present for interactive edits and absent on an API-format reload, so scrubbing `inputcount` deliberately does NOT reflow the slots. `WidgetHandle.on('change', listener)` passes `(value, oldValue)` only — the bridge drops the trailing args when calling `notify`. Converting the guard away makes every interactive scrub of `inputcount` add/remove input slots immediately, which changes the node's input list in the saved workflow. NEEDED: an origin/source discriminator on the change listener (e.g. a third arg distinguishing user edit from programmatic/configure-time set).

Collapsed `hideWidgetForGood` from the twelve-line converted-widget hack to `widget.setHidden(true)`. Gone with it: the `origType`/`origComputeSize`/`origSerializeValue` save-and-restore (nothing in this pack ever read them back, so the widget could never be un-hidden), the `[0,-4]` computeSize magic number, the `widget.type` overwrite — `type` is identity, and hiding was always the real intent — and the `suffix`/`linkedWidgets` recursion, which existed only to propagate the mangled type string. This helper has zero callers anywhere in the pack, so no caller is stranded; the remaining thirteen exports (chainCallback, getSlotPos, clientToCanvas, watchImageInputs, …) are untouched and keep their signatures for the siblings still importing them.
files.test:
equivalence: Calling the pack's hide helper on a node's widget makes that widget stop occupying space on the node while leaving its value untouched, and leaves every other widget on the node visible. Passes on both the original (widget.type = "converted-widget", computeSize = () => [0,-4]) and the converted source (node.widgets.get(name).setHidden(true)). The other exports of this module — chainCallback, makeUUID, clientToCanvas, getNodeAtPoint, typesCompatible, getSlotPos, addMiddleClickPan, resolveSourcePreview, watchImageInputs, captureVideoFrame, rectHitTest, cursorForBboxMode, addWheelPassthrough — keep identical signatures and behaviour, so every importing sibling in the pack still resolves.

fix: A widget hidden by this helper must still be written into the saved workflow's widgets_values, and the node's widget list must still report it. On the ORIGINAL this fails: the helper overwrites `widget.type` with the string "converted-widget" + suffix, which is identity, so any code that branches on the widget's type (including the pack's own combo/number handling and litegraph's serializer path for converted widgets) no longer sees the real type, and the saved `origType`/`origComputeSize`/`origSerializeValue` bookkeeping is dead weight that nothing in this pack ever reads back to restore it — the widget can never be un-hidden. On the CONVERTED source `setHidden(true)` is presentation only: `widgetType` still reports the real type, the value is retained and serialized, and `setHidden(false)` restores it.

files.detail: Wraps `app.canvas.onRenderBackground` to paint the whole graph background with a tiled OffscreenCanvas pattern, returning true to suppress LiteGraph's own clear+grid pass. The published API has no canvas-level rendering surface at all: `widgets.canvas` is per-node, and there is no `comfy.ui`. It also needs the extension-registration surface — `settings`, `commands`, `menuCommands` and `app.ui.settings.getSettingValue/setSettingValue` — none of which exist on `Comfy` (version/supports/require/capabilities/forMajor/sameEntity/adopt/graph/defs only). Missing: (1) a graph-background render hook, (2) published settings/commands/keybindings registration.

Its core is injecting "Add SetNode"/"Add GetNode" into the SLOT connection dropdown, done by wrapping `app.canvas.showConnectionMenu` and temporarily swapping the `LiteGraph.ContextMenu` constructor to splice an entry in after "Add Reroute". `b.addMenuItem` covers node context menus only; canvas-wide and slot menus are explicitly still a gap. It also exports `addNode(name, nextTo, options)` on `window.kjNodes` — positioning a new node relative to a neighbour via `nextTo.pos`/`nextTo.size` and auto-wiring the first free slot — consumed by setgetnodes.js, which is itself unconvertible. Missing: (1) slot/connection-menu contribution, (2) settings registration.

Auto-wires the current selection by scoring candidate slot pairs on 2D screen distance. `comfy.graph.selection()` covers the selection read, but the scoring needs each slot's canvas-space position via `getSlotPos` -> `node.getConnectionPos`/`getInputPos`/`getOutputPos`, and `SlotCollection`/`InputSlotHandle` expose no geometry whatsoever. It also needs `LiteGraph.isValidConnection` for the type-compatibility tier, `commands`/`keybindings` registration for its 'f' hotkey, and `app.extensionManager.toast`. Missing: (1) slot positions on a slot handle, (2) a published type-compatibility check, (3) commands/keybindings registration, (4) toast.

`fixNode` is precisely `graph.replaceNode(id, newType, {widgets, keepPosition})` — snapshot the old node, create a fresh one of the same comfyClass, restore widget values by name, reconnect inputs and outputs by slot name, delete the old one, roll back on throw. `graph.replaceNode` is specified in docs/node_api_WIP.md but is NOT implemented: `GraphHandle` in v1/comfy-api.d.ts has only node/nodes/nodesOfType/add/remove/links/selection. Hand-rolling it against the published API is also impossible — it needs `node.serialize()`, `LiteGraph.createNode`, and reconnection driven by raw link ids read from `app.graph.links`. Missing: `graph.replaceNode`.

Drop-a-node-onto-a-wire insertion. It samples each link's bezier at 20 points against the dragged node's bounding box using a hand-reimplemented control-point offset that must match what LiteGraph draws, sets LiteGraph's internal `link._dragging` flag to hide the real wire, and paints an animated dashed ghost link into the shared canvas context via `chainCallback(lgCanvas, 'onDrawForeground')` with a per-frame `setDirty(true, false)` rAF loop. Link-curve hit-testing, the canvas-wide foreground context and a runtime flag on an LLink have no equivalent under Nodes 2.0 or ECS. Needs the author.

Hold-S-and-drag to swap two nodes. Detects overlap by walking `graph._nodes` back-to-front comparing `pos`/`size` boxes, paints a pulsing glow around the target by wrapping `lgCanvas.onDrawBackground` with `Date.now()`-driven repaints, and animates the position exchange differently depending on `LiteGraph.vueNodesMode` (CSS transform on `[data-node-id]` vs a per-frame rAF writing `node.pos`). The swap itself also disconnects and rebuilds every link via `disconnectInput`/`connect`, which allocates new link ids and would change the serialized workflow. Canvas-draw-order-dependent chrome plus renderer-mode branching; needs the author.

A renderer performance panel that monkey-patches the canvas itself: it replaces `LGraphCanvas.prototype`-level instance methods `canvas.draw` (aliasing `bgcanvas`/`bgctx` onto the foreground canvas while `dragging_canvas` is true) and `canvas.renderInfo` (blitting a cached offscreen FPS overlay), and writes the global `LiteGraph.ROUND_RADIUS`, `canvas.render_shadows`, `canvas.render_connections_border`. Every one of these is a renderer internal deliberately excluded from the published API, and the whole feature is meaningless once the canvas renderer is replaced. Needs the author.

A pointer gesture: shake a selected node to break its links. It samples `lgCanvas.selectedItems` and node `pos` on every `pointermove`, scales deltas by `lgCanvas.ds.scale` to detect direction reversals in screen pixels, and gates on canvas internals (`connecting_links`, `resizing_node`, `node_widget`) to tell a node drag from a widget drag. The bypass pass then walks raw links via `graph.getLink`, `disconnectInput(i, true)` and `connect(slot, node, slot, link.parentId)` — reconnection through parentId has no published form. A canvas-pointer gesture over canvas drag state has no destination under Nodes 2.0; needs the author.

Paints a `?` glyph into the node's foreground with `ctx.translate`/`scale`/`fillText` in a patched `nodeType.prototype.onDrawForeground`, hand-hit-tests clicks against that glyph's box in `onMouseDown` (returning true to swallow the event), and then positions a DOM popup every frame by composing `ctx.getTransform()` with the canvas bounding rect and `devicePixelRatio` into a DOMMatrix. That is a hand-painted interactive canvas control whose placement is derived from the graph's own transform — `widgets.canvas` draws in its own element and cannot read the graph transform, and there is no published mouse hook on a node. The file's second half (MutationObserver injecting a `?` button into `.lg-node-header`) already targets Nodes 2.0, so the right outcome is for the author to drop the canvas half rather than for us to guess.

The SetNode/GetNode virtual-node system, and by far the pack's deepest coupling. It declares `class SetNode extends LGraphNode` / `class GetNode extends LGraphNode` with `isVirtualNode = true` and registers them through `LiteGraph.registerNodeType`; `defs.define({execution:'frontend', resolve})` is the destination in principle, but the surrounding machinery has none: it patches four `LGraphCanvas.prototype` methods (`computeVisibleNodes`, `_processMiddleButton`, `createDefaultNodeForSlot`, `showLinkMenu`), builds its own `LiteGraph.ContextMenu` for the Constant combo with per-entry border colours read from `canvas.default_connection_color_byType` and `LGraphCanvas.link_type_colors`, overrides the widget's `onClick` to hand-hit-test increment/decrement zones against `canvas.ds.scale`, branches throughout on `LiteGraph.vueNodesMode` and `app.configuringGraph`, and drives dynamic retyping from `onConnectionsChange` with `LiteGraph.INPUT`/`OUTPUT` constants. (The reported widgets.splice finding at 999-1000 is only the cache-invalidation hack inside `_refreshComboOptions`, which alone would be a clean `setOption('values', ...)`.) This is the pack's flagship feature and needs the author, not a patch.

The node captures a getDisplayMedia stream and ships the cropped frame to Python by installing a transforming serializer: `frameWidget.serializeValue = () => { serializeCtx.drawImage(video, sx, sy, sw, sh, ...); return serializeCanvas.toDataURL('image/png') }`. `WidgetDef.serialize` is a boolean only and `b.onSerialize` explicitly cannot write core fields such as widgets_values, so there is no way to substitute a computed value for a widget at serialize time — dropping it would send an empty frame_data to the backend, a prompt-visible change. Secondary gaps in the same file: `frameWidget.computeSize = () => [0,-4]` (that part is `setHidden(true)`), and `btnWidget.name = '🔴 0:07 - Stop capture'` mutating a button's label per second (`setLabel` exists but on-node button widgets have no published click callback at all — see jsnodes.js). Missing: a per-widget transforming serializer.

2,058 lines / 96KB in a single `beforeRegisterNodeDef`. Structurally it is one convertible construct — a `chainCallback`-driven node with one `addDOMWidget('crop_preview', 'CropPreviewWidget', wrapper)` at line 365 that would become `widgets.mount` — but essentially the entire file is the interactive transform editor inside that widget (crop/rotate/scale handles, hit-testing, video frame capture, `watchImageInputs` on the IMAGE inputs). Converting it responsibly means reading all of it to be sure nothing else touches the graph; splitting the registration out is a small, safe patch that a human should make with the file in front of them.

2,701 lines / 157KB — the largest file in the pack by a wide margin, a whole prompt-builder UI (style palette, canvas layout, element editor) behind one `beforeRegisterNodeDef`. It additionally hits the same blocker as jsnodes.js and screencap_stream.js: `elementsWidget.serializeValue = () => {...}` at line 1476 installs a transforming serializer to cache-bust a wired import, and `WidgetDef.serialize` is boolean-only with no published equivalent. So even at a workable size it would be an api-gap punt for that one line; at this size it needs the author.

skillNotes.claim: `node.widgets.add({ type: 'button', ... })` has nowhere to put the click handler — `WidgetDef` has no `callback` and `WidgetHandle.on('change')` provably never fires for a button, so any `addWidget("button", label, null, fn)` is an api-gap, not a conversion.
skillNotes.evidence: comfyui-kjnodes jsnodes.js has three button sites — setupDynamicInputs' `this.addWidget("button", "Update inputs", null, rebuild)`, the `Set all` button on FluxBlockLoraSelect/Wan21BlockLoraSelect, and SoundReactive's `Start mic capture`/`Stop mic capture`. `WidgetDef` in widgetHandle.ts is `{type,name,value?,options?,disabled?,hidden?,serialize?}` with no callback member, and the `on('change')` bridge routes through `notify`, which starts `if (value === previous) return`. A button click invokes litegraph's callback without mutating `widget.value`, so previous === value and the listener is skipped. `NodeDefBuilder.addMenuItem` is a context-menu entry, not an on-node button, so it is not a substitute.

skillNotes.claim: `widget.on('change', ...)` passes only `(value, oldValue)`, so a pack that branched on litegraph's second `canvas` argument to tell an interactive edit from a programmatic/reload-time set loses that distinction — check every captured `widget.callback` for a second parameter before converting it.
skillNotes.evidence: comfyui-kjnodes jsnodes.js `setupDynamicInputs` does `countW.callback = function (value, canvas) { ...; if (!canvas) rebuild(); }` with the comment "the canvas arg from interactive edits is the tell, so scrubbing the count doesn't reflow the node". The bridge in widgetHandle.ts calls `notify(w, value, previous)` and drops `...rest`, so the trailing canvas argument never reaches the listener. Converting literally makes every interactive scrub of `inputcount` add/remove input slots, which changes the node's `inputs` array in the saved workflow.

skillNotes.claim: `node.inputs.add(name, type)` accepts no third options argument and `SlotPatch` carries only `{name, label, type}`, so the `{shape: 7}` optional-slot marker that "Multi" combiner packs pass to `addInput` has no published destination and is a wire-format loss, since slot `shape` is serialized in the node's `inputs` array.
skillNotes.evidence: comfyui-kjnodes jsnodes.js calls `setupDynamicInputs(this, { type: "IMAGE", prefix: "image_", slotOptions: {shape: 7} })` for ImageBatchMulti, ImageAddMulti, CrossFadeImagesMulti, TransitionImagesMulti, ImageConcatMulti and JoinStringMulti, reaching `node.addInput(name, type, slotOptions)`. In comfy-api.d.ts `SlotCollection.add` is declared `add(name: string, type: string): THandle` and `SlotPatch` is `{ name?, label?, type? }` — shape appears nowhere on the slot surface (only `NodeHandle.getShape/setShape`, which is the node's shape, not a slot's).

skillNotes.claim: `WidgetDef.serialize` being a boolean covers only "omit this value" — a pack that assigned a *transforming* `widget.serializeValue = () => f(widget.value)` is an api-gap, because the transformed value is what reaches the backend prompt, not just the saved workflow.
skillNotes.evidence: comfyui-kjnodes jsnodes.js, cases SaveImageKJ / SaveImageWithAlpha / SaveStringKJ / DecodeAndSaveVideo / ModelSaveKJ / LoraExtractKJ: `widget.serializeValue = () => applyTextReplacements(app, widget.value)` on `filename_prefix`. Dropping it sends `%date:yyyy-MM-dd%`-style tokens to the backend unexpanded and changes the filename written to disk. `NodeDefBuilder.onSerialize` cannot stand in — its doc states it merges only keys the pack owns and that core fields are not writable from there, so it cannot rewrite `widgets_values`. `applyTextReplacements` is itself only reachable via `window.comfyAPI.utils` and has no published equivalent.

skillNotes.claim: The `no-silently-dropped-writes` check rejects `node.widgets.get(name)?.setHidden(true)` — the exact line widgets.md currently prints as the ✓ example — so a helper that hides a widget must take the WidgetHandle as a parameter (`function hide(node, widget) { widget.setHidden(true) }`) and let its caller do the lookup, rather than looking the widget up itself behind `?.`.
skillNotes.evidence: Converting `hideWidgetForGood` in ComfyUI-KJNodes `web/js/utility.js:32`. The reference's "Never let a write vanish" section contrasts `comfy.graph.node(id)?.widgets.get(name)?.setHidden(true)` (✗) with `node.widgets.get(name)?.setHidden(true)` (✓, "use the handle you were given"), but the harness flags the second too: `1 write(s) behind an optional chain: ?.setHidden(`. The distinction the check actually enforces is not "did you look the NODE up" but "is any write optional-chained at all". Dropping the widget lookup into the signature passed both checks with a smaller diff than adding an explicit guard.

skillNotes.claim: Before punting a whole pack's canvas-UX files one at a time, check whether they are blocked on the *extension registration* surface rather than on the graph API: `settings`, `commands`, `keybindings`, `menuCommands` and `app.ui.settings.getSettingValue/setSettingValue` have no published destination at all, so any file whose feature is a user-toggleable canvas behaviour is an `api-gap` punt regardless of how convertible its graph calls look.
skillNotes.evidence: Six of ComfyUI-KJNodes' 25 files (canvas_background.js, fillconnect.js, node_insert.js, nodeswap.js, performance.js, shake_to_disconnect.js) are each a hotkey or toggle registered through `app.registerExtension({ settings, commands, keybindings })` and read back with `app.ui.settings.getSettingValue(...)`. `Comfy` in v1/comfy-api.d.ts exposes only version/major/supports/require/capabilities/forMajor/sameEntity/adopt/graph/defs — there is no `ui`, no `extensions`, no settings or command registry — so even the parts with clean destinations (`canvas.selected_nodes` → `comfy.graph.selection()` in fillconnect.js) cannot be reached, because nothing can turn the feature on.
